mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) compresses discount rates for equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors seek yield in equities.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (p-value > 0.05 in t-test vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: When annualized CPI inflation exceeds 2.5%, the market anticipates aggressive monetary tightening, causing S&P 500 20-day forward returns to decline as risk assets are sold.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 2.5% (p-value > 0.05 in t-test vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in unemployment rate and declines in residential sales signal a broad-based economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint negative signal (UNRATE rising and RSAFS falling) fails to predict negative returns in more than 40% of cases (Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: During post-shock recovery phases, persistently low federal funds rates stimulate economic activity and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of post-shock recovery periods (p-value > 0.05 in t-test vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Strong monthly job growth (PAYEMS above 100k) indicates robust economic expansion, driving corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months with PAYEMS growth above 100k (p-value > 0.05 in t-test vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production exceeding 1.0% signals an imminent economic slowdown, causing S&P 500 20-day forward returns to turn negative as investors reduce risk exposure.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO monthly change is below -1.0% (p-value > 0.05 in t-test vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in housing starts and residential sales indicate a weakening housing market, which typically precedes broader economic weakness and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint negative signal (HOUST and RSAFS declining) fails to predict negative returns in more than 40% of cases (Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS above 3.0%), the S&P 500 experiences negative 60-day forward returns due to reduced liquidity and higher discount rates for equities.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 3.0% (p-value > 0.05 in t-test vs baseline).
